title: Enforce the never-change-meaning rule for every beautification edit
body:
## Context
Beautification ({{SN-BTY-001}}) keeps the user's own handwriting and makes it neater — it is not ink-to-text ({{SN-HWR-007}}). That promise only holds if the feature **can never silently change what someone wrote**. This issue turns that rule into a machine-checked invariant rather than a review convention, and it is the gate every other beautification issue depends on.

The *mechanics* of reversibility already exist elsewhere in the epic: {{SN-BTY-002}} models beautification as a reversible derived overlay on the original ink and {{SN-BTY-012}} wires it into undo/redo. This issue adds the thing neither provides — a decision, per edit, about **whether the edit is allowed to happen without asking**, and the audit fields that make that decision provable after the fact.

Two edit classes exist and the code must be able to prove which one it is applying:

- **Class G — geometric tidying.** Baselines straightened, slant and letter size made consistent, word/line spacing normalised, lists and margins aligned, drifting lines pulled level. The recognised character sequence of the region is unchanged. May apply silently, and only at the user's chosen intensity ({{SN-BTY-042}}).
- **Class C — content-altering.** Anything that changes the recognised character sequence: a spelling correction, a word substitution, an inserted or removed glyph, a case change on a case-sensitive token. **Never silent.** Always a visible, reversible affordance the user accepts per word.

ADR-0016 §5 already states "recognition never mutates the document silently"; decision 4 gives us the non-destructive object model to honour it. Apple's Smart Script and Goodnotes' spellcheck both split refine (silent) from correct-spelling (tap a flagged word) — we make the split enforceable.

## Scope
**In:** the `BeautifyEdit` taxonomy and classifier; the before/after recognition comparison that decides the class; the hard gate that refuses to commit a Class C edit without a user decision token; the per-edit audit fields added to the overlay record of {{SN-BTY-002}}; the review-affordance contract (badge, per-word accept/reject) that {{SN-BTY-013}}'s preview and {{SN-BTY-012}}'s undo hang off.
**Out:** the derived-overlay/undo machinery itself ({{SN-BTY-002}}, {{SN-BTY-012}}); the geometric transforms ({{SN-BTY-004}}–{{SN-BTY-008}}) and the style re-render engine; protected regions ({{SN-BTY-039}}); the adversarial corpus that exercises this gate ({{SN-BTY-038}}); the intensity control ({{SN-BTY-011}}, {{SN-BTY-042}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For every candidate edit the engine recognises the affected word region **before and after** and compares NFC-normalised token sequences; any difference (including case and diacritics) classifies the edit `contentAltering`.
- [ ] A `contentAltering` edit **cannot** reach the document without a `UserDecision` token: the commit API requires it, an assertion fires in debug, and `app/test/security/beautify_no_silent_content_change_test.dart` proves no code path bypasses it.
- [ ] Class G edits leave the recognised token sequence identical on ≥ 99.5 % of words in the evaluation corpus ({{SN-BTY-044}}); any word where it diverges is reverted to untouched ink and counted as a defect.
- [ ] No edit of either class is proposed for a word whose recognition confidence is < 0.85 unless the user selected that word explicitly.
- [ ] Every applied edit extends {{SN-BTY-002}}'s overlay record with `{editId, class, recognisedBefore, recognisedAfter, decidedBy, intensity, engineVersion, modelVersion}`; a round-trip test asserts that reverting through {{SN-BTY-012}} restores the original stroke geometry **byte-identical** to its pre-beautify serialisation.
- [ ] A document reopened after revert serialises byte-identically to the pre-beautify `.sanenote`.
- [ ] Classification costs ≤ 8 ms per word on the mid-Android reference device and runs off the UI isolate; it never touches the wet-ink path.
- [ ] Batch beautify of a page reports a single summary ("12 words tidied · 2 spellings need your OK") and is one undo step.

## Technical notes
`packages/sane_ml/lib/src/beautify/edit_classifier.dart` exposes a sealed `BeautifyEdit` (`GeometryOnly` | `ContentAltering`) and `classify(region, before, after) → Result<BeautifyEdit, Failure>`; callers pattern-match with Dart 3 `switch` (no exceptions across package boundaries, CLAUDE.md §6). Recognition comes from the `InkRecognizer` interface of {{SN-HWR-002}}; where the region is untouched, reuse the cached tokens from background recognition ({{SN-HWR-006}}) instead of a second inference. Persistence rides on {{SN-BTY-002}}'s derived overlay — the original stroke is never destructively overwritten (docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §10.1; decision 4) — so this issue only adds fields to that record and a guard in front of its commit function. The review affordance lives in `app/lib/features/editor/beautify/`; the commit path is `packages/sane_core` ops. Do not hop isolates on the draw path (CLAUDE.md §8): classification runs on a one-shot `Isolate.run`.

## Security & privacy
A silent content change to a person's own record is an integrity failure (OWASP-A08 software & data integrity failures) and a LINDDUN *Unawareness* harm; add the row to docs/security/threat-model.md. Recognised text, token sequences and the audit record are **note content**: stored locally, E2E-encryptable on sync, never logged (MASVS-STORAGE-1, CWE-117). Entirely on-device; no cloud path in this issue — a cloud recogniser is only ever reachable through the per-request opt-in of {{SN-HWR-019}}. Fail closed: if recognition fails, the edit is not applied.

## UX notes
Class C words carry a non-colour-only flag (dotted underline + icon) per docs/design/accessibility.md; tapping opens a sheet with the original ink, the proposal rendered in the user's own hand, per-word Accept/Keep mine, and "Never for this word" (feeds {{SN-HWR-016}}). Class G applies live with a brief, Reduce-Motion-aware cross-fade. Tokens only from `sane_ui`; correct in all 17 looks and dark. Empty/error state: "Couldn't read this clearly — left as you wrote it."

## Test plan
`packages/sane_ml/test/beautify/edit_classifier_test.dart` (class decision, NFC/case/diacritic sensitivity, confidence floor), `packages/sane_core/test/beautify_undo_roundtrip_test.dart` (byte-identical restore), `app/test/security/beautify_no_silent_content_change_test.dart` (negative/abuse: no commit path without a decision token), golden `app/test/golden/beautify_flagged_word_*` across looks, and a perf test asserting the ≤ 8 ms/word budget.

## Dependencies
SN-BTY-002 (reversible derived overlay this gate guards), SN-HWR-002 (recogniser interfaces), SN-HWR-006 (cached recognised tokens), SN-CORE-003 (CRDT revisions for non-destructive edits). Undo behaviour lands in {{SN-BTY-012}}; preview in {{SN-BTY-013}}. Parent epic {{SN-BTY-001}}.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (dart format, dart analyze --fatal-infos, arch-lint, unit/widget/golden, Semgrep, mobsfscan, gitleaks/trufflehog, OSV-Scanner, dependency-review)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed (docs/adr/0016-on-device-ml-and-ai.md, docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §10, docs/security/threat-model.md)
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md; no note content, recognised text, style features or ink coordinates in logs

title: Build the do-not-correct adversarial corpus and gate spelling changes on it
body:
## Context
The fastest way to destroy trust in handwriting beautification is to "correct" something that was right. A student writes *eigenvector*, *H2SO4*, *Nguyễn*, *getUserById*, *kya haal hai*, or a deliberately misspelled brand name, and the app helpfully turns it into something else. Goodnotes ships a Personal Dictionary precisely because spellcheck over handwriting false-positives constantly; Samsung's spell/grammar pass has the same exposure.

This issue builds the adversarial fixture set that the meaning-preservation gate ({{SN-BTY-037}}) is measured against, and wires it into CI as a blocking budget. It is the empirical half of the safety rule: {{SN-BTY-037}} proves *a correction cannot be silent*, this proves *a correction is rarely wrong in the first place*.

## Scope
**In:** the labelled `doNotCorrect` / `shouldOffer` corpus; the evaluation runner; the false-positive budget and its CI gate; the fixture licence/consent manifest.
**Out:** the misspelling detector and its dictionary-aware suppression ({{SN-BTY-026}}) and the in-ink correction flow ({{SN-BTY-027}}, {{SN-HWR-017}}) — this issue measures them, it does not build them; the custom dictionary feature ({{SN-HWR-016}}); the general recognition accuracy harness ({{SN-HWR-020}}), which this extends rather than duplicates.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Corpus contains ≥ 600 labelled items across **≥ 10 adversarial classes**: proper nouns and personal names (including transliterated Indian names), place names, technical and scientific jargon, code identifiers and snippets (`getUserById`, `x += 1`, `#include <stdio.h>`), chemical formulae and units (`H2SO4`, `C6H12O6`, `9.8 m/s²`), inline equations and Greek symbols, invented/coined words, deliberate misspellings and dialect spellings, abbreviations and student shorthand (`w/`, `b/c`, `∴`, `->`), and code-switched / mixed-script text (Hinglish, Latin+Devanagari on one line).
- [ ] Coverage spans ≥ 3 scripts and both pen and finger input so the gate is not Latin-and-stylus only.
- [ ] The pipeline proposes a correction for **≤ 0.5 %** of `doNotCorrect` items; exceeding the budget fails CI.
- [ ] Recall on the `shouldOffer` set (genuinely misspelled words) may not fall more than 2 points below the committed baseline — the gate cannot be passed by simply never correcting anything.
- [ ] Every proposal that does fire is asserted to be a Class C edit routed through the {{SN-BTY-037}} affordance; a proposal applied silently fails the suite.
- [ ] Words present in the custom dictionary ({{SN-HWR-016}}) are never proposed — 0 exceptions.
- [ ] Fixtures are synthetic or consent-recorded; no real user notes; each item carries source, licence and consent in `manifest.json`.
- [ ] The PR-scope run completes in ≤ 90 s and is deterministic (3 consecutive runs byte-identical).

## Technical notes
Fixtures under `tools/eval/beautify_corpus/do_not_correct/` as stroke-sample JSON (the `InkSample` shape of docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §1.2) plus ground-truth text, so they exercise the online-ink path rather than image OCR. Runner in `packages/sane_ml/test/beautify/do_not_correct_eval_test.dart`, loading through the shared loader added by {{SN-BTY-044}}; results emitted to `beautify_quality_report.json` consumed by the CI gate ({{SN-BTY-046}}). Use the mock `InkRecognizer` for deterministic unit runs and the real ML Kit adapter ({{SN-HWR-003}}) in the nightly device-lab job. Budgets live in the machine-readable baseline file, not in code.

## Security & privacy
Fixtures are test data, but they are handwriting: keep them out of the app bundle and out of crash/diagnostic payloads. No real user content without a recorded consent record (GDPR/DPDP lawful basis; decision 8). The runner must not log recognised text on failure — it reports item ids and class counts only (CWE-117). No network access in the PR-scope job.

## UX notes
None beyond baseline (test infrastructure), except one user-facing consequence this gate protects: a wrongly flagged word must always be dismissible with "Keep mine", and repeated dismissals of the same token offer "Add to my dictionary" ({{SN-HWR-016}}).

## Test plan
`packages/sane_ml/test/beautify/do_not_correct_eval_test.dart` (budget assertions per class, not just in aggregate — a class may not be sacrificed to keep the average), `packages/sane_ml/test/beautify/dictionary_suppression_test.dart`, plus a fixture-integrity test asserting every item has ground truth, class label, licence and consent fields.

## Dependencies
SN-BTY-037 (edit classification the corpus asserts against), SN-BTY-026 (the detector under test), SN-HWR-016 (custom dictionary suppression). Corpus tooling is shared with {{SN-BTY-044}}; gate wiring is {{SN-BTY-046}}.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (dart format, dart analyze --fatal-infos, arch-lint, unit/widget/golden, Semgrep, mobsfscan, gitleaks/trufflehog, OSV-Scanner, dependency-review)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed (docs/adr/0016-on-device-ml-and-ai.md, docs/product/prd-02-library-documents-audio-search.md §11)
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md; no note content, recognised text, style features or ink coordinates in logs

title: Never beautify protected regions and hand maths to the math pipeline
body:
## Context
Some ink must never be touched, however messy it looks. A **signature** is legally meaningful *because* it is idiosyncratic. A **sketch or diagram** is not writing and "straightening" it vandalises it. **Maths** has its own pipeline ({{SN-HWR-014}}) where a straightened superscript or a normalised minus sign changes the expression. **Annotations on a legal or exam PDF** are evidence. Shape snapping already lives in {{SN-HWR-012}} and must own diagram strokes exclusively.

This issue defines the protected-context set, the detector that routes ink away from the text beautifier, and the explicit per-region opt-out that lets the user say "leave this as I wrote it" anywhere else. Without it, {{SN-BTY-037}}'s guarantee ("meaning is preserved") is true per-word but useless per-document.

## Scope
**In:** the protected-context taxonomy and detector; hand-off of maths regions to {{SN-HWR-014}} and diagram strokes to {{SN-HWR-012}}; the document-level and region-level exclusion model (CRDT-synced, exported in `.sanenote`); the exclusion UI (lasso → "Never beautify this", page, notebook, template default); the PDF-annotation policy flag.
**Out:** the math and shape engines themselves and the sketch routing pass ({{SN-BTY-034}}); reflow boundaries, which are a different question — {{SN-BTY-031}} stops a corrected word from disturbing *unrelated* ink, this issue stops beautification from *touching* ink at all; the strength setting ({{SN-BTY-011}}, {{SN-BTY-042}}); locked-notebook behaviour, which already excludes derived processing ({{SN-GCMP-002}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Text-vs-non-text classification reaches precision ≥ 0.97 for "this is a drawing" on the evaluation corpus ({{SN-BTY-044}}); drawing clusters are never beautified.
- [ ] Signature-like clusters (long connected stroke, high curvature entropy, isolated on the page, near a "Sign"/"Signature" label or inside a signature field) are never beautified — **0 false beautifications** on the 100-signature fixture.
- [ ] Maths regions route to {{SN-HWR-014}} and are never baseline-straightened, slant-normalised or re-spaced by the text path; superscripts, subscripts and fraction bars keep their vertical relationships exactly.
- [ ] Annotations on a PDF whose notebook carries `annotationPolicy: legalOrExam` default beautification **off**; enabling it shows a one-line reason and is recorded per notebook.
- [ ] A lasso selection can be marked "Never beautify this"; the exclusion is a document property (LWW register) that survives CRDT merge ({{SN-CORE-003}}), sync, `.sanenote` export/import and page reflow.
- [ ] Exclusion scopes compose predictably: object > page > notebook > profile default; the effective value is inspectable in one tap and covered by a truth-table unit test.
- [ ] An excluded region shows a subtle, non-colour-only marker **only while the beautify tool is active**, never in normal reading or export.
- [ ] Detection adds ≤ 15 ms per page of 2,000 strokes, runs off the UI isolate and caches per page until strokes change.

## Technical notes
Detector in `packages/sane_ml/lib/src/beautify/protected_regions.dart`, consuming the R-tree page index and stroke clustering from `packages/sane_ink` (docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §7) plus recognition segmentation from {{SN-HWR-006}}; features include stroke-length distribution, curvature entropy, aspect ratio, intersection density, recognition confidence and the ML Kit shape/gesture classifier signal used by {{SN-HWR-012}}. Exclusions are stored as a `beautifyPolicy` prop on `Page`/`Notebook` and a `beautifyExcluded` flag on objects in `packages/sane_core` (decision 4). Lasso entry point extends {{SN-ED-004}}'s selection menu in `app/lib/features/editor/`. PDF annotation layers follow docs/adr/0014-pdf-engine.md — the policy flag lives on the notebook, not the PDF.

## Security & privacy
Protecting signatures and exam/legal annotations is an integrity control (OWASP-A08) and a real-world-harm control: a modified signature or exam answer is a forgery risk. Default-deny for the ambiguous case — when the detector is unsure, do not beautify. Region policy is note content: local, E2E-encryptable, never logged (MASVS-STORAGE-1, CWE-117). No cloud path. Add the "beautifier alters evidentiary ink" row to docs/security/threat-model.md.

## UX notes
Design refs: docs/design/screens-and-flows.md §7 (lasso object menu) and §12 (recognition). Marker is a hairline dashed outline plus a small lock glyph — never colour alone (docs/design/accessibility.md). Copy: "Left as you wrote it — this looks like a signature." Settings → Handwriting & stylus exposes the notebook default. Works in all 17 looks and dark; Reduce Motion honoured.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_ml/test/beautify/protected_regions_test.dart` (classifier precision on fixtures; signature fixture 0-false-positive assertion), `packages/sane_core/test/beautify_policy_merge_test.dart` (CRDT merge + scope truth table), `app/test/widget/beautify_exclusion_menu_test.dart`, golden `app/test/golden/beautify_excluded_marker_*`, and an integration test that a legal/exam PDF notebook never auto-beautifies.

## Dependencies
SN-BTY-037 (edit gate), SN-ED-004 (lasso selection), SN-CORE-003 (CRDT props). Hand-offs: {{SN-HWR-012}} shapes, {{SN-HWR-014}} math.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (dart format, dart analyze --fatal-infos, arch-lint, unit/widget/golden, Semgrep, mobsfscan, gitleaks/trufflehog, OSV-Scanner, dependency-review)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed (docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §9, docs/adr/0014-pdf-engine.md, docs/security/threat-model.md)
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md; no note content, recognised text, style features or ink coordinates in logs

title: Add the tremor-aware beautification profile for Parkinson’s and essential tremor
body:
## Context
Handwriting beautification is one of the strongest inclusive-design wins in a note app, and tremor is the clearest case. Essential tremor sits roughly in a 4–12 Hz band and Parkinsonian tremor roughly 3–7 Hz; both ride on top of an intended trajectory the writer executed correctly. Removing the band while keeping the trajectory gives someone back *their own* handwriting, legible — which is exactly the maintainer's brief, and something no competitor ships (Samsung straightens, Apple refines, neither targets tremor).

We already have a capture-time aid: the Motion Filter in {{SN-INK-003}} / docs/design/pen-and-brush-spec.md §8, off by default. That is a live filter with a latency budget. This issue is the **post-hoc** pass: it can afford a full-stroke, two-pass, frequency-domain analysis that a real-time filter cannot, and it must not double-apply with the live filter.

## Scope
**In:** tremor detection from the persisted per-point stream; band-selective smoothing that removes tremor energy without flattening intended curvature; amplitude-tolerant parameterisation of the existing size and spacing passes ({{SN-BTY-006}}, {{SN-BTY-007}}) for tremulous input; the combined-strength budget shared with {{SN-INK-003}}; a "Steady my writing" entry in the accessibility range ({{SN-BTY-042}}).
**Out:** the live capture filter ({{SN-INK-003}}); the generic stroke-regularisation pass ({{SN-BTY-008}}), which this feeds rather than replaces; dysgraphia letter-form work ({{SN-BTY-041}}); the strength UI itself ({{SN-BTY-011}}, {{SN-BTY-042}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Detection: compute the residual between the raw centreline and a fitted low-order trajectory, take its band energy over 3–12 Hz using the per-point `tMicros` clock, and classify a stroke as tremor-affected when band energy exceeds the writer-relative threshold; precision ≥ 0.9 on the synthetic-tremor corpus ({{SN-BTY-044}}) where ground truth is known by construction.
- [ ] At the "Strong" setting, composite legibility ({{SN-BTY-045}}) improves ≥ 25 % and on-device recognition accuracy improves **≥ 15 points absolute WER** on the synthetic-tremor bands.
- [ ] Intended curvature is preserved: deliberate loops, circles and descenders keep ≥ 0.9 curvature-RMS ratio versus the clean source; a hand-drawn circle is never flattened into a line.
- [ ] Once the style guard of {{SN-BTY-047}} exists, style similarity stays above its floor at every strength — steadying must not generify; until then the same property is checked by the ink-preservation metric of {{SN-BTY-045}}.
- [ ] Double-smoothing guard: with the {{SN-INK-003}} motion filter enabled, the combined smoothing applied to a stroke never exceeds the configured ceiling; a unit test asserts the composed amount, and the UI states that the two dials share one budget.
- [ ] Works with **no downloaded model** (pure geometry, Tier 0 of {{SN-BTY-049}}) so it is available on every device including web and low-end Android.
- [ ] A 2,000-stroke page completes in ≤ 3 s on the mid-Android reference device, off the UI isolate, cancellable, with progress.
- [ ] Every change is Class G under {{SN-BTY-037}} (the recognised text must be identical) or it is not applied.

## Technical notes
Implement in `packages/sane_ink/lib/src/beautify/tremor.dart` (pure Dart, no `package:flutter`) so it is testable headless and reusable by the geometric tier: resample the stored decimated centreline to uniform time using `tMicros` (docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §10.1 keeps per-point timestamps), fit a smoothing spline / Savitzky–Golay trend, FFT or Goertzel the residual for the 3–12 Hz band, attenuate that band, and reconstruct. Reuse the existing 1€ filter parameters and the Motion-Filter semantics from `packages/sane_ink/lib/src/filter/` rather than inventing a second vocabulary. The combined ceiling lives in the pen preset's `stabilise` block (docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §4.2). Never run on the wet stroke (CLAUDE.md §8).

## Security & privacy
Tremor is **health-adjacent inference about the user**. The tremor classification and any per-writer threshold are derived personal data: keep them on-device, per-profile, out of logs and telemetry (only coarse, non-identifying buckets may ever be counted, and only under {{SN-BTY-052}}), exclude them from sync and backup by default, and make them deletable in one tap with the rest of the handwriting model ({{SN-BTY-050}}). Never surface a diagnosis-shaped string anywhere in UI or code comments; the setting is "Steady my writing", not a condition label. MASVS-PRIVACY-1; LINDDUN *Identifiability*/*Disclosure* rows in docs/security/threat-model.md.

## UX notes
Lives in Settings → Accessibility beside the motor-assist presets ({{SN-A11Y-013}}) and in the beautify strength sheet ({{SN-BTY-042}}), with a **live before/after preview** on the user's own recent line (a11y requirement carried over from pen-and-brush-spec §8). Never auto-enabled. Announce results via the status announcer ({{SN-GA11-002}}): "Steadied 14 words." Reduce Motion: cross-fade, no morph.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_ink/test/beautify/tremor_test.dart` (band attenuation on synthesised signals with known spectra; curvature preservation; determinism), `packages/sane_ml/test/beautify/tremor_quality_test.dart` (legibility/WER deltas against the corpus), `packages/sane_ink/test/beautify/combined_smoothing_budget_test.dart`, golden `app/test/golden/beautify_tremor_before_after_*`, plus a perf test for the 3 s page budget.

## Dependencies
SN-INK-003 (stabilisation/motion filter and its parameters), SN-BTY-037 (Class G assertion). Metrics from {{SN-BTY-045}}; corpus from {{SN-BTY-044}}.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (dart format, dart analyze --fatal-infos, arch-lint, unit/widget/golden, Semgrep, mobsfscan, gitleaks/trufflehog, OSV-Scanner, dependency-review)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed (docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §2, docs/design/pen-and-brush-spec.md §8, docs/design/accessibility.md)
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md; no note content, recognised text, style features or ink coordinates in logs

title: Add dysgraphia and dyspraxia profiles with personal letter-form normalisation
body:
## Context
Dysgraphia and dyspraxia produce a different pattern from tremor: not high-frequency wobble but **inconsistency** — the same letter drawn at four sizes on one line, words drifting off the baseline, wildly variable word gaps, mixed upper- and lower-case, slant that changes mid-word, and overshoot at stroke joins from motor-planning cost. Readers (including the writer, a week later) lose the text to that variance, not to any single malformed letter.

Beautification fixes exactly this class of problem, and it is the "structure" half of the maintainer's brief — "the spelling or structure". The critical constraint: normalise toward **the writer's own median form**, never toward a typeface and never toward a population average. A student with dysgraphia should get their handwriting back, tidied — not somebody else's. {{SN-BTY-020}} already learns the writer's glyphs, slant, spacing and pressure; this issue is the pair of **profiles** that point the existing slant, size, baseline and spacing passes at that per-glyph median instead of at a page-level estimate, plus the variance targets that make the result readable.

## Scope
**In:** the dysgraphia and dyspraxia profiles; per-glyph variance targets driving {{SN-BTY-004}}–{{SN-BTY-007}} from {{SN-BTY-020}}'s learned model; the minimum-evidence rule before a glyph is normalised at all; join/overshoot cleanup; optional letter-spacing expansion for readability; per-notebook override.
**Out:** learning the writer's glyph model ({{SN-BTY-020}}) and its store ({{SN-BTY-019}}); the underlying transforms ({{SN-BTY-004}}–{{SN-BTY-008}}); tremor ({{SN-BTY-040}}); the style-similarity guard that polices this work ({{SN-BTY-047}}); reading aids for consuming text, which are {{SN-A11Y-014}}'s reading mode; spelling ({{SN-BTY-026}}, {{SN-BTY-027}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Normalisation uses the per-character median form from {{SN-BTY-020}}, matched to ink through the stroke↔text mapping of {{SN-HWR-006}}; a character with fewer than **12 observed instances** is left completely alone (minimum-evidence rule), and the rule is unit-tested per character class.
- [ ] Inter-word gap variance is reduced ≥ 40 % while intra-word gaps change by ≤ 10 % — words become separable without letters being pulled apart; bimodality of the gap distribution improves measurably ({{SN-BTY-045}}).
- [ ] Ascender/descender and x-height ratios stay within ±15 % of the writer's own median — the profile equalises variance, it does not impose a norm.
- [ ] Baseline re-seating brings word-centroid RMS deviation below 0.15 × x-height per line without changing word order or line breaks.
- [ ] Any case change (e.g. a mid-word capital) is **Class C** under {{SN-BTY-037}} and always offered, never applied — capitalisation carries meaning (initialisms, chemical symbols, code).
- [ ] Style similarity ({{SN-BTY-047}}) ≥ the configured floor at every strength; failing the guard reverts the word.
- [ ] Composite legibility improves ≥ 20 % on the synthetic-dysgraphia bands of {{SN-BTY-044}} with recognition WER not worse than before.
- [ ] Profiles are selectable in Settings → Accessibility and per notebook, are off by default, and are announced when applied.

## Technical notes
Profiles live in `packages/sane_ml/lib/src/beautify/profiles/dysgraphia.dart` as parameter vectors over the existing passes; the geometry they drive stays in `packages/sane_ink/lib/src/beautify/` so the pure-Dart path remains reusable by the no-model tier ({{SN-BTY-049}}). Where a median glyph template is compared against an instance, reuse the $P/$Q resample-scale-translate preprocessing already used for shapes (docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §9.2) and a robust per-point geometric median rather than a mean, so outliers do not drag the target. Normalisation is an affine plus local warp applied to the stored centreline; the pen preset and brush dynamics are untouched so the stroke still renders with the user's own pen (docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §4). All persisted per-writer state belongs to {{SN-BTY-019}}'s encrypted style store and is covered by {{SN-BTY-022}}/{{SN-BTY-050}} deletion — this issue adds no new storage.

## Security & privacy
The per-writer letter-form model this consumes is a **biometric-adjacent identifier** — handwriting is used for identity verification — and is governed by {{SN-BTY-019}}'s encrypted local store and {{SN-BTY-050}}'s confinement and deletion rules; this issue must not copy, cache or export any of it outside that store. Selecting a "dysgraphia" profile is health-adjacent: store the selection as an opaque preference id, keep condition wording out of telemetry and logs, and use neutral UI copy. MASVS-PRIVACY-1; LINDDUN *Identifiability* row in docs/security/threat-model.md.

## UX notes
Settings → Accessibility presents outcomes, not diagnoses: "Even letter size", "Steady baseline", "Clear word spacing", grouped under "Make my writing easier to read", with live before/after on the user's own page. Non-colour-only cues; 44 pt / 48 dp targets; all 17 looks + dark; Reduce Motion honoured. Copy follows docs/design/accessibility.md tone rules.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_ml/test/beautify/dysgraphia_profile_test.dart` (minimum-evidence rule, no cross-character leakage, parameter vectors), `packages/sane_ink/test/beautify/variance_targets_test.dart` (gap/ratio/baseline assertions), `packages/sane_ml/test/beautify/dysgraphia_quality_test.dart` (corpus deltas), golden `app/test/golden/beautify_dysgraphia_*`, and a negative test that a case change never auto-applies.

## Dependencies
SN-BTY-020 (learned per-glyph model this profile points at), SN-BTY-037 (Class C routing for case), SN-HWR-006 (stroke↔text mapping). Guarded by {{SN-BTY-047}}; measured by {{SN-BTY-045}}.

## Definition of done

title: Expose beautification strength as an accessibility setting with an extended range
body:
## Context
{{SN-BTY-011}} builds the beautify intensity control with per-notebook and per-action scope — the everyday, aesthetic dial. This issue takes that control and does the accessibility work on top of it, which is a different problem: the right setting for someone who wants tidy-looking notes is not the right setting for someone with limited fine-motor control who needs legibility above all, and the ceiling that keeps writing from looking uncanny for the first user is exactly the ceiling that fails the second.

So the default ladder stays conservative, and the **accessibility range goes further than the default allows**, deliberately trading some character for legibility when the user asks for it. This issue also owns the part {{SN-BTY-011}} cannot: making the control **and the review of what changed** fully operable by screen reader, switch and keyboard, and composing the dial with the stabilisation slider ({{SN-INK-003}}) and the motor-assist presets ({{SN-A11Y-013}}) so the user sees one coherent system rather than three competing dials.

## Scope
**In:** the preset ladder and the default cap; the Settings → Accessibility unlock of the extended range; the shared smoothing budget with {{SN-INK-003}}; the accessible review list of what changed; full screen-reader / switch / keyboard operability of both.
**Out:** the intensity control, its scoping and persistence ({{SN-BTY-011}}); the before/after preview widget ({{SN-BTY-013}}), which this reuses; the transforms themselves ({{SN-BTY-040}}, {{SN-BTY-041}}, {{SN-BTY-004}}–{{SN-BTY-008}}); telemetry for tuning defaults ({{SN-BTY-052}}); onboarding discovery ({{SN-BTY-051}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] {{SN-BTY-011}}'s 0–100 intensity gains presets **Off / Light / Balanced / Strong / Maximum legibility**; Balanced is the default and the default ladder is capped at Strong.
- [ ] "Maximum legibility" is reachable only by enabling the extended range in Settings → Accessibility; it is never the default, is never turned on by an app update, and reverts to nothing on a settings reset ({{SN-SET-016}}).
- [ ] Presets interpolate a documented parameter vector across the transforms of {{SN-BTY-004}}–{{SN-BTY-008}} (baseline, slant, size, gap, join) rather than a magic number per feature; the mapping table is unit-tested and lives in one file.
- [ ] {{SN-BTY-013}}'s before/after preview, driven from this control on the user's own most recent line, updates within **150 ms** of a change and never blocks input.
- [ ] The control exposes Semantics (name, role, value, and a value-text like "Balanced, 3 of 5"), is operable by keyboard, switch and Voice Control ({{SN-A11Y-010}}), has 44 pt / 48 dp targets and ≥ 4.5:1 contrast in all 17 looks and dark mode.
- [ ] After a beautify pass the status announcer ({{SN-GA11-002}}) announces a content-free summary ("12 words tidied, 2 spellings need your OK") and a focusable **review list** walks each change with Accept / Keep mine, reachable without gestures ({{SN-A11Y-009}}).
- [ ] The extended-range flag round-trips per profile via {{SN-SET-003}} and composes with {{SN-BTY-011}}'s per-notebook scope; the effective value is inspectable in one tap.
- [ ] The screen states in one line that stabilisation ({{SN-INK-003}}) and beautification share a combined smoothing budget, and changing one updates the other's displayed effective value.
- [ ] Reachable from the editor in ≤ 3 taps, and from Settings → Handwriting & stylus ({{SN-SET-007}}).

## Technical notes
Preset ladder and the accessibility cap extend {{SN-BTY-011}}'s model in `packages/sane_core/lib/src/settings/` (immutable value object; preferences via {{SN-SET-003}}); UI in `app/lib/features/settings/` using the `SaneSettingRow` composite from {{SN-SET-004}} and `sane_ui` tokens only (no hardcoded colours — CLAUDE.md §9). The preview widget comes from {{SN-BTY-013}} and must be driven by the same transform pipeline as the real pass so preview and result cannot diverge. The extended-range unlock is a preference, not a build flag, and must be announced and reversible.

## Security & privacy
None beyond baseline for the control itself; the preference is per-profile local state ({{SN-SET-003}}), excluded from logs. The one privacy-relevant detail: the preview renders the user's own note content, so it must not be captured in screenshots taken by diagnostics, and the preference value may only reach telemetry as a coarse bucket under {{SN-BTY-052}} (MASVS-PRIVACY-1).

## UX notes
Design refs: docs/design/screens-and-flows.md (Settings tabs), docs/design/pen-and-brush-spec.md §8 (the smoothing dial this sits beside), docs/design/accessibility.md. Copy is outcome-led ("Make my writing easier to read"), never diagnosis-led. Empty state when there is no recent handwriting to preview: a clearly labelled sample. Error state: "Couldn't preview — your writing is untouched." Reduce Motion: cross-fade the preview rather than animating strokes.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_core/test/settings/beautify_strength_ladder_test.dart` (ladder mapping, cap, unlock, reset), `app/test/widget/beautify_strength_control_test.dart` (semantics, keyboard/switch traversal, announcement text), `app/test/widget/beautify_review_list_test.dart` (gesture-free accept/reject), golden `app/test/golden/beautify_strength_sheet_*` across 17 looks + dark, and a perf test on the 150 ms preview budget.

## Dependencies
SN-BTY-011 (the intensity control this extends), SN-A11Y-013 (motor-assist presets to compose with), SN-INK-003 (shared smoothing budget), SN-BTY-037 (review affordance contract). Preview from {{SN-BTY-013}}; persistence via {{SN-SET-003}}; surfaces in {{SN-SET-007}}.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (dart format, dart analyze --fatal-infos, arch-lint, unit/widget/golden, Semgrep, mobsfscan, gitleaks/trufflehog, OSV-Scanner, dependency-review)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed (docs/design/accessibility.md, docs/design/pen-and-brush-spec.md §8)
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md; no note content, recognised text, style features or ink coordinates in logs

title: Tune beautification for one-handed and phone-sized handwriting
body:
## Context
On a phone, handwriting is at its worst and beautification is at its most valuable. People write with a thumb or fingertip, one-handed, on a canvas a few centimetres wide, often standing up; there is no pressure signal (`pressureIsReal == false`, docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §1.2), the contact patch is large and imprecise, and letters come out huge, sloped and crowded. The same person writing on an iPad with a Pencil produces completely different ink. A profile tuned for tablet-plus-stylus under-corrects phone writing and puts the affordances where a thumb cannot reach.

Sane Notes ships five surfaces in lock-step (PRD-LB §1.2), so "beautify works on phones" is not optional polish — it is parity.

## Scope
**In:** a phone/finger profile that retunes the existing baseline, size and spacing passes ({{SN-BTY-004}}, {{SN-BTY-006}}, {{SN-BTY-007}}) for finger input; the finger path for tidy-on-lift ({{SN-BTY-009}}); behaviour inside the zoom-writing box; reflow of tidied words within a narrow measure without reordering; one-handed reachability of every beautify affordance; the Tier-3 phone latency budget.
**Out:** the transforms and the real-time refine loop themselves ({{SN-BTY-004}}–{{SN-BTY-009}}); the phone editor layout ({{SN-PHN-001}} family); the strength ladder ({{SN-BTY-042}}); tier resolution ({{SN-BTY-049}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With finger input (no real pressure), composite legibility ({{SN-BTY-045}}) improves ≥ 20 % on the phone bands of {{SN-BTY-044}} with **no change to word order or line breaks**.
- [ ] Reflow after tidying re-wraps to the page measure only; a word never moves to a different line index unless the user asked for reflow explicitly, and the change is one undo step.
- [ ] Every beautify affordance (apply, strength, review, undo) is operable within the one-handed reach zone — bottom 40 % of the screen — at 6.7" and on a folded foldable ({{SN-DIM-001}} layout classes), verified by a widget test at those metrics.
- [ ] A single line tidies in ≤ 400 ms on the Tier 3 reference phone ({{SN-PERF-004}}), off the UI isolate, and never during an active stroke.
- [ ] Writing inside the zoom box is tidied on commit with no visible jump of already-committed ink; a golden frame test captures the commit frame.
- [ ] The phone profile is selected by a runtime capability/pointer-kind probe (finger vs stylus), not a platform string, and a stylus on a phone gets the tablet profile.
- [ ] Works at Tier 0 (no model) so it is available on every supported phone and on mobile web ({{SN-BTY-049}}).
- [ ] Battery: tidying 20 lines costs ≤ 0.1 % battery on the reference phone (measured with the {{SN-PERF-013}} protocol).

## Technical notes
Profile parameters live beside the other presets in `packages/sane_ink/lib/src/beautify/profiles.dart`; selection uses `PointerDeviceKind` plus the capability probe pattern of {{SN-INK-029}} (never a platform check — CLAUDE.md §8). Where pressure is absent, width/dynamics come from velocity (docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §3.3), so the tidy pass must preserve the velocity-derived width envelope or strokes will visibly change weight. Reflow reuses the line-model produced by {{SN-HWR-006}} segmentation; it operates on object transforms (LWW registers) rather than re-serialising geometry. Zoom-box integration hooks the commit path in `app/lib/features/editor/`.

## Security & privacy
None beyond baseline. The pointer-kind probe and profile choice are device state, not content; they must not be logged with any content and may reach telemetry only as a coarse bucket under {{SN-BTY-052}}.

## UX notes
Design refs: docs/design/screens-and-flows.md (phone editor, zoom-writing box) and the adaptive-layout rules in CLAUDE.md §9. Affordance: a small "Tidy line" chip appears in the thumb zone after lift, dismissible, never covering the caret or the last word written. Copy is short enough for a 400 px width. All 17 looks + dark; Reduce Motion honoured; RTL mirrored.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_ink/test/beautify/phone_profile_test.dart` (finger vs stylus selection; width-envelope preservation), `app/test/widget/beautify_reach_zone_test.dart` (affordances inside the reach zone at phone and folded metrics), `packages/sane_ml/test/beautify/phone_quality_test.dart` (corpus deltas, no reordering), golden `app/test/golden/beautify_zoombox_commit_*`, and a Tier 3 perf test for the 400 ms budget.

## Dependencies
SN-BTY-042 (strength model and affordances), SN-BTY-049 (capability tiers, Tier 0 guarantee). Measured with {{SN-BTY-044}}/{{SN-BTY-045}}.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (dart format, dart analyze --fatal-infos, arch-lint, unit/widget/golden, Semgrep, mobsfscan, gitleaks/trufflehog, OSV-Scanner, dependency-review)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed (docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §3, docs/platform/performance-budgets.md)
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md; no note content, recognised text, style features or ink coordinates in logs

title: Assemble the labelled messy-handwriting corpus with synthetic tremor
body:
## Context
Every claim beautification makes — "more legible", "still looks like you", "never changes meaning" — is unfalsifiable without a corpus. {{SN-HWR-020}} already builds recognition-accuracy datasets for the recogniser; this issue extends that harness with the data beautification specifically needs: **messy** handwriting across bands of legibility, across scripts and input devices, plus synthetically degraded samples where the clean ground truth is known exactly so improvement can be measured rather than eyeballed.

Synthetic degradation is the key trick. Recording genuinely tremulous or dysgraphic handwriting at scale is slow and ethically heavy; taking clean samples and applying a parameterised, seeded degradation (band-limited tremor, size jitter, baseline drift, slant jitter, gap jitter) gives thousands of items whose *correct* output is literally the pre-degradation sample.

## Scope
**In:** the corpus contents, manifest and licensing/consent record; the seeded degradation generator; the shared loader; human legibility ratings and their reliability check; CI fetch/verify plumbing.
**Out:** the metrics computed over it ({{SN-BTY-045}}); the CI gate ({{SN-BTY-046}}); the do-not-correct adversarial set ({{SN-BTY-038}}), which uses this loader but has its own labels.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ≥ 2,000 labelled lines from ≥ 40 writers, stratified into **5 legibility bands**, covering ≥ 4 scripts (Latin, Devanagari, Arabic/RTL, CJK), stylus **and** finger input, phone **and** tablet capture, and left- and right-handed writers.
- [ ] A seeded degradation generator produces tremor (band-limited 3–12 Hz with amplitude and coherence parameters), size jitter, baseline drift, slant jitter and gap jitter; identical seed ⇒ byte-identical output; every generated item links to its clean source.
- [ ] Every item carries: raw `InkSample` stream with `tMicros`, ground-truth text, writer id, script, device/pointer kind, handedness, condition tags, and a **human legibility rating** (5-point).
- [ ] Human ratings use ≥ 3 raters per item with inter-rater reliability **Krippendorff α ≥ 0.7**; items below threshold are re-rated or dropped, and α is recorded in the manifest.
- [ ] Provenance: every item is synthetic **or** carries a recorded consent and licence entry; zero real user notes without one; a fixture-integrity test fails the build on a missing field.
- [ ] Corpus is content-addressed and versioned; CI verifies hashes before use; it is **excluded from the app bundle** and from any release artifact (asserted by a bundle-size/content test).
- [ ] A fast PR subset (≤ 200 items, ≤ 90 s) and a full nightly set are both defined and selectable by the runner.
- [ ] Documented in docs/product/ and referenced from the beautification section so a new agent can regenerate the synthetic half from scratch.

## Technical notes
Layout: `tools/eval/beautify_corpus/{clean,degraded,phone,scripts}/` with a top-level `manifest.json` (schema versioned) and per-item JSON in the `InkSample` shape of docs/architecture/ink-engine.md §1.2. Generator in `tools/eval/bin/degrade_ink.dart` (pure Dart, seeded `Random`), sharing the tremor synthesis model with {{SN-BTY-040}}'s tests so the generator and the fixer cannot silently diverge. Loader in `packages/sane_ml/test/support/beautify_corpus.dart` built on the deterministic fixture factories from {{SN-QA-011}}. Large binaries are fetched by a CI step with hash verification, never committed raw if they exceed the repo policy.

## Security & privacy
Handwriting samples are personal data and are handwriting-biometric-adjacent. Store consent records with the fixtures; support withdrawal (an item can be removed and the baseline re-cut); never ship the corpus in a build; never send it anywhere. The runner logs item ids and aggregate counts only — no recognised text, no sample coordinates (CWE-117). Real-writer items are pseudonymised by writer id with the mapping kept out of the repo. GDPR/DPDP lawful-basis note recorded with the DPIA template ({{SN-PRV-013}}).

## UX notes
None beyond baseline — internal evaluation asset. One indirect user-facing requirement: the corpus must include the writing of people with tremor and dysgraphia (synthetic at minimum, consented real samples where available from the accessibility sessions of {{SN-GA11-025}}), or the accessibility claims of {{SN-BTY-040}}/{{SN-BTY-041}} cannot be substantiated.

## Test plan
`tools/eval/test/degrade_ink_test.dart` (determinism, parameter ranges, clean↔degraded linkage), `packages/sane_ml/test/support/beautify_corpus_test.dart` (loader, stratification counts, manifest schema), a fixture-integrity test asserting consent/licence/ground-truth completeness, and a release test asserting the corpus is absent from built artifacts.

## Dependencies
SN-HWR-020 (recognition eval harness this extends), SN-QA-011 (deterministic fixture factories). Consumed by {{SN-BTY-038}}, {{SN-BTY-045}}, {{SN-BTY-046}}, {{SN-BTY-047}}.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed (docs/product/prd-02-library-documents-audio-search.md §11, docs/security/threat-model.md)
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md; no note content, recognised text, style features or ink coordinates in logs
